title: Design Instagram (photo-sharing)
relevance: High — canonical 45-min "Design Instagram / photo-sharing" HLD at Meta PA, FAANG, Snap/Pinterest cousins, and Indian product cos; probes media pipeline (presign → object store → CDN) plus hybrid feed fan-out (same celebrity cliff as Twitter/News Feed).
company_notes: Campus/new-grad: extremely common; expected signal is presigned media + CDN and hybrid fan-out + Redis ID timelines + async workers, not Meta’s full ranking stack. Experienced/Meta PA/mid: deeper probes on celebrity threshold, media variants, reconstruction, delete/privacy, multi-DC, graph hotspots, light ranking. Top-tier product HLD; sister prompts are News Feed/Twitter timeline (hq04), Dropbox-style large blobs, and YouTube.

phases.goal: Scope upload + follow + home/profile feed; state NFRs and cut Stories/Reels/Explore unless asked.

must_hit.point: In-scope FRs: upload photo (optional short video) + caption to followers; uni-directional follow/unfollow; reverse-chronological paginated home feed; profile posts grid.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists upload, follow, home feed, and profile grid and explicitly excludes Stories/Reels/DMs/Explore unless asked.

must_hit.point: NFR: feed p99 after hydrate ~200–500 ms (Hello Interview <500 ms); photos up to ~8 MB; CDN for global image delivery; availability over strong feed consistency with few-seconds lag OK.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States a sub-500 ms feed target, multi-MB photo size, CDN delivery, and eventual feed freshness.

must_hit.point: Scale framing example: 500M DAU and ~100M posts/day (Hello Interview), or own numbers used consistently.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Anchors design to 500M DAU / 100M posts/day or states and sticks to alternative assumptions.

must_hit.point: Out of scope unless asked: likes/comments (counters only if asked), hashtag search, Stories TTL, Reels ABR, ads, full ranking.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cuts ranking/Stories/Reels/ads explicitly and offers to return if interviewer wants them.

probes: What is in scope for a 45-minute Instagram design, and what do you cut?
What latency and consistency targets are you designing the home feed for?

hints.1: Treat this as two products: media plane plus social/feed plane.
hints.2: Say upload + follow + home/profile feed in; Stories, Reels, Explore, DMs, and full ranking out unless asked.
hints.3: NFRs: feed p99 ~200–500 ms after hydrate, photos up to ~8 MB via CDN, availability over strong consistency with few-seconds lag; scale example 500M DAU / ~100M posts/day.

phases.goal: Use round numbers from the prompt to justify async writes, CDN for media, hybrid fan-out, and ID-only feed cache.

must_hit.point: 100M posts/day ≈ ~1.2K writes/s average with 5–10× peak; avg photo ~200–500 KB raw → tens of TB/day before variants, and 3–5 resized variants multiply storage.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Derives ~1.2K write/s from 100M posts/day and notes multi-TB media growth with 3–5 variants.

must_hit.point: Each DAU opens home ~10×/day → billions of reads/day in the 100K+ QPS class; image GETs are higher still → CDN, not API.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates feed QPS (100K+) from even higher image GETs and concludes CDN owns media delivery.

must_hit.point: Avg ~200–500 followers vs celebrities at 10M–100M makes pure push write amplification the cliff.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts hundreds of followers with 10M–100M celebrity followership to motivate hybrid fan-out.

must_hit.point: Home cache: 800 × ~16–24 B IDs ≈ ~15–20 KB/user; active users in Redis imply multi-TB RAM, so store IDs only.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Computes ~15–20 KB per user from ~800 ID slots and argues against storing full post objects in the timeline.

probes: Walk the write QPS and media storage from ~100M posts/day.
Why can’t every follower’s home timeline store full post objects in Redis?

hints.1: Pick the Hello Interview 100M posts/day framing and stick to it.
hints.2: Estimate write QPS, raw+variant storage, feed open rate → 100K+ QPS, and celebrity follower amplification.
hints.3: 100M posts/day ≈ ~1.2K writes/s (5–10× peak); ~200–500 KB photos → tens of TB/day with 3–5 variants; ~10 home opens/DAU → 100K+ QPS; celebrities 10M–100M break pure push; 800 IDs × ~16–24 B ≈ ~15–20 KB/user.

phases.goal: Define REST upload-session/complete, follow, profile, and cursor-paginated feed APIs without proxying image bytes.

must_hit.point: Upload flow: POST /v1/posts/upload-session → {post_id, presigned_urls[], expires_at}; POST /v1/posts/{post_id}/complete with caption marks uploaded and enqueues processing; GET/DELETE /v1/posts/{post_id}.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes upload-session returning presigned URLs, then complete to enqueue processing, not PUT body through API.

must_hit.point: Social/read APIs: POST/DELETE /v1/follows; GET /v1/users/{user_id}/posts?cursor=&limit= for profile; GET /v1/feed?cursor=&limit= for home feed returning Post[].
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists follow endpoints plus cursor/limit profile and home feed GETs.

must_hit.point: Cursor is last time-sortable post_id, not OFFSET; client fetches image bytes directly from CDN, not through the API; auth from token, never trust user_id in body for “me”.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects OFFSET, uses post_id cursors, and keeps media GETs on CDN with token-based auth.

probes: How does the client upload a multi-MB photo without melting the API tier?
How do you paginate the home feed safely under concurrent inserts?

hints.1: API should talk metadata and URLs, not photo bytes.
hints.2: Split upload-session (presign) from complete (caption + enqueue); feed/profile use cursor + limit.
hints.3: POST upload-session → presigned_urls; POST complete; GET feed/profile with cursor=last post_id; client loads images from CDN.

phases.goal: Separate post metadata, follow graph, ID-only home timelines, and object-storage/CDN media keys.

must_hit.point: Post metadata DB: post_id PK, author_id, caption, status uploading/processing/ready, media CDN URLs, created_at; shard by post_id or author_id for profile locality.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Models posts with status machine and CDN URLs in DB, bytes elsewhere.

must_hit.point: Follow graph stores follower→followee plus reverse index; home timeline cache is Redis list/ZSET home:{user_id} of post IDs capped ~800 with LTRIM/ZREMRANGEBYRANK.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows dual follow indexes and Redis home timelines of IDs capped around 800.

must_hit.point: User/profile timeline is posts by author_id + time/post_id (celebrity pull source); post/user object caches hydrate after ID fetch; object storage keys raw/{post_id} and var/{post_id}/{size}.webp with CDN origin on processed bucket.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates profile timeline, hydration caches, and immutable variant keys in object storage + CDN.

probes: What lives in Redis home timelines versus the metadata DB versus object storage?
Why do you need both a followers and a following index?

hints.1: Metadata and blobs are different stores; feeds hold IDs only.
hints.2: Entities: User, Post/Media, Follow, HomeTimeline cached IDs; status uploading→processing→ready.
hints.3: Postgres-style post metadata + Redis home:{user_id} of ~800 post IDs + follow graph both ways + S3/CDN immutable variant keys; hydrate post:{id}/user:{id}.

phases.goal: Draw upload/publish with presign + media workers + async fan-out, and read path with Redis IDs, celebrity merge, hydrate, CDN URLs.

must_hit.point: Upload/publish: Client→LB→API creates post metadata uploading + presign → client uploads to object storage → complete → MQ → media workers resize/encode variants → status ready → post.published → fan-out workers → Graph Service; if not celebrity, LPUSH/ZADD into active followers’ Redis homes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks presign→direct upload→async media processing→ready→async fan-out, skipping celebrity push.

must_hit.point: Read/feed: Client→LB→Feed Service reads Redis home IDs, pulls recent posts from celebrity followees’ user timelines, merge/sort by id/time, hydrate post+user from cache/DB, return page with CDN URLs; client renders from CDN.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes ID fetch + celebrity pull merge + batch hydrate + CDN URLs on the response.

must_hit.point: Boxes: stateless API, media workers, Post/User service, Graph service, fan-out workers, Feed/Timeline service, Redis timeline cluster, metadata DB + caches, object storage, CDN, MQ (Kafka-class).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the service boxes including Redis timelines, graph, fan-out workers, object store, and CDN.

probes: Walk me through publish from camera roll to a follower’s home feed.
What happens on a home feed refresh for a user who follows both normal accounts and celebrities?

hints.1: Never put photo bytes on the API hot path; fan-out after ready is async.
hints.2: Two paths: upload/presign/media workers/fan-out write path, and Redis+celebrity-merge+hydrate read path.
hints.3: API presigns → client PUT to object store → media workers → ready → fan-out workers push post_id to non-celebrity followers’ Redis; feed service merges Redis IDs with celebrity pulls, hydrates, returns CDN URLs.

phases.goal: Defend hybrid fan-out, presigned upload, eager variants, async idempotent fan-out, and eventual feed consistency with read-your-writes for authors.

must_hit.point: Hybrid fan-out: push for normal accounts; skip push for celebrities above a follower threshold (~10K–1M, ops-tuned); at read merge precomputed timeline + recent celebrity posts.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names push for normals, pull for whales above an ops-tuned ~10K–1M threshold, and read-time merge.

must_hit.point: Presigned direct upload beats proxying multi-MB photos through API (auth simpler on proxy but melts app servers/bandwidth); short-lived URLs are the expected pattern.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects API proxy upload and argues short-lived presigned client→blob PUT.

must_hit.point: Eager common image variants on upload (interviews usually eager 2–4 sizes) vs lazy rare sizes; sync fan-out never blocks publish HTTP—use at-least-once MQ workers with idempotent timeline inserts deduped by post_id.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Chooses eager 2–4 sizes and async idempotent fan-out workers instead of sync Redis storms.

must_hit.point: Feed is eventually consistent; read-your-writes for author via profile timeline/optimistic UI; media not visible in feed until status ready.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Accepts seconds of feed lag, author sees own post on profile, and feed only after ready.

probes: Push, pull, or hybrid—what do you choose for Instagram and why?
Should the publish HTTP request wait until every follower’s Redis list is updated?

hints.1: Celebrity write amplification is the reason pure push fails.
hints.2: Compare push vs pull costs, then land on hybrid with a named threshold and merge.
hints.3: Push normals; skip celebrities above ~10K–1M; merge at read; presign uploads; eager 2–4 variants; MQ fan-out with idempotent post_id inserts; feed eventually consistent until ready.

phases.goal: Scale CDN/origin, fan-out lag, celebrity partitions, Redis homes, graph, hydration, and media workers.

must_hit.point: Viral media: edge TTL + origin shield + immutable content-hash URLs; don’t invalidate whole trees on caption edits; aim for 95%+ media hits at edge.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Protects origin with CDN TTL/shield/immutable URLs and cites 95%+ edge hit goal.

must_hit.point: Fan-out workers/MQ lag: scale consumer groups, skip inactive users, prioritize active followers, alert on lag, DLQ poison posts; celebrities skip push and paginate huge follower lists.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Tunes fan-out consumers, skips cold users, and pulls celebrities instead of pushing.

must_hit.point: Redis timeline cluster sharded by user_id; reconstruct on miss from graph + post store; cap length; don’t keep cold homes forever; graph caches hot follower lists with dual indexes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shards Redis by user_id, reconstructs misses, caps/evicts cold homes, caches hot follower lists.

must_hit.point: Hydration via batch multi-get + post cache; shard metadata by author for profile; avoid giant SQL JOINs per refresh; media workers autoscale on queue depth with idempotent processing and quarantine of failed encodes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Batch-hydrates, avoids follower×posts SQL JOINs, and autoscales idempotent media workers.

probes: A post goes viral—what protects object-storage origin?
An inactive user comes back after months with an empty Redis home—what do you do?

hints.1: CDN and hybrid fan-out exist because read QPS and celebrity writes dominate.
hints.2: Separate bottlenecks: CDN/origin, fan-out lag, Redis shard, graph hotspot, hydration, media queue.
hints.3: Immutable CDN URLs + origin shield (95%+ edge); skip cold/celebrity push; shard Redis by user_id and reconstruct misses; batch hydrate; autoscale media workers on queue depth.

tradeoffs.topic: Push vs pull vs hybrid fan-out
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Push gives fast scroll but celebrity write storms and inactive waste; pull is cheap to write but slow at high follow counts; hybrid pushes normal accounts, skips celebrities above an ops-tuned ~10K–1M threshold, and merges precomputed timeline with recent celebrity posts at read—the expected production answer.

tradeoffs.topic: Presigned direct upload vs proxy through API
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Proxying simplifies auth but melts app-server CPU/bandwidth on multi-MB photos; API issues short-lived presigned (or session) URLs and the client PUTs directly to object storage—the expected pattern.
Eager generation of common sizes on upload gives fast first paint everywhere at CPU/storage cost; lazy/on-demand rare sizes save work but hurt cold latency; interviews usually eager 2–4 sizes.
Never block publish HTTP on millions of Redis writes; use at-least-once MQ/workers with idempotent timeline inserts deduped by post_id rather than inventing exactly-once delivery.
Home feed is eventually consistent with few-seconds lag OK; authors get read-your-writes via profile timeline or optimistic UI; media stays out of feed until status is ready.

gotchas.trap: Designing pure push for a celebrity with 100M followers
gotchas.correction: Skip push for those accounts; pull recent posts from the celebrity’s user timeline and merge at read time.

gotchas.trap: Uploading photo bytes through the app/API server
gotchas.correction: Issue presigned/direct-to-blob upload URLs; keep the API on metadata and orchestration only.

gotchas.trap: Storing full images or captions in every home timeline entry
gotchas.correction: Store post/media IDs only (~hundreds / ~800), hydrate post+user objects in batch, serve bytes from CDN URLs.

gotchas.trap: Ignoring delete, unfollow, mute, or private-account semantics after push
gotchas.correction: Push copies go stale—filter at hydrate or async-remove, and run privacy checks before serving.

gotchas.trap: Fan-out forever to inactive users / empty Redis on return
gotchas.correction: Skip cold users; on miss run a reconstruction job from graph + post store instead of retaining cold homes forever.
OFFSET breaks under inserts; cursor on time-sortable post_id (Instagram-style 64-bit or Snowflake).

gotchas.trap: SQL JOIN followers × posts on every home refresh
gotchas.correction: Dies at read QPS; use only to motivate precomputed ID timelines + hydration.
Different TTLs, ABR, or ML retrieval—mention only if asked; keep scope on upload + follow + home/profile.

gotchas.trap: Claiming exactly-once fan-out from the MQ
gotchas.correction: Say at-least-once delivery plus idempotent ZADD/dedupe by post_id; don’t invent exactly-once MQ magic.
